## Summary

Decomposed the `requests` HTTP library (19 Python source files, ~6,400 LOC) into **12 Logical Units**:

**Domain units** (what the library is about):
- `request-response-model` — Request/PreparedRequest/Response data model
- `session` — Session + one-shot `get()`/`post()`/etc. convenience functions
- `auth` — Basic/Digest HTTP authentication schemes
- `exceptions` — the error/warning hierarchy

**Infra units** (how it talks to the world):
- `transport-adapter` — urllib3-backed socket/TLS transport
- `cookies` — cookie jar adaptation
- `structures` — CaseInsensitiveDict/LookupDict + the status-code table
- `hooks` — the response-hook dispatch mechanism
- `http-utils` — proxy/netrc/encoding/header helper toolbox + CA bundle lookup
- `foundation` — Python/urllib3 compat shims, tiny string helpers, version metadata, legacy import aliasing
- `diagnostics` — `requests.help` bug-report tool
- `package-init` — `__init__.py`'s import-time compatibility checks and public-namespace assembly

Reconciliation folded several single-caller or grab-bag files together (e.g., `api.py` into `session`, `certs.py` into `http-utils`, five tiny plumbing modules into `foundation`) per the merge test, rather than leaving one-unit-per-file. All 19 source files are either owned by a unit or explicitly excluded (tests, docs, packaging/CI config); one `violations_observed` entry flags `auth.py` reaching directly into a live connection object instead of going through a transport-adapter entrypoint.
